results.content: After initial approval, and at periodic intervals during the course of the study, the DSMB responsibilities are to: • Provide input to assist NIDDK in protecting the safety of the study participants; • Provide input to the NIDDK on major changes to the research protocol, informed consent documents and plans for data and safety monitoring; • Provide input to the NIDDK on the progress of the study, including periodic assessments of data quality and timeliness, participant recruitment, accrual and retention, participant risk versus benefit, performance of the study sites, and other factors that may affect study outcomes; • Review areas of concern regarding the performance of individual sites and provide comment to the NIDDK on actions to be considered regarding sites that perform unsatisfactorily; • Consider factors external to the study when relevant information becomes available, such as scientific or therapeutic developments that may have an impact on the safety of the participants or the ethics of the study; • Provide input to the NIDDK on modification of the study protocol or possible early termination of the study because of attainment of study objectives, safety concerns, low likelihood of showing a benefit of the intervention, or inadequate performance (such as enrollment and retention problems); • If appropriate, review the interim analysis of efficacy in accordance with stopping rules which are clearly defined in the protocol and have the approval of the NIDDK with concurrence of the DSMB; • Provide input to the NIDDK on the desirability of proceeding to the full-scale study at the completion of a feasibility phase, if appropriate; • Provide input to the NIDDK on the potential impact of ancillary studies on the integrity of the parent study; and • Monitor clinical ancillary studies unless an independent DSMB is established or NIDDK determines that a DSMB is not required.

results.content: Emory IRB Guidance Version 1/11/2022 Data Safety Monitoring Boards What is a DSMB? A Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) is an independent group of experts that advises the sponsor and the study investigators. Independence is essential to ensure that DSMB members are objective and capable of an unbiased assessment of the study's safety and efficacy data. In addition, the DSMB should: • Provide written documentation confirming review of the protocol and agreement with the study design and the data safety monitoring plan (DSMP). • Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) – Who will review safety data, consider stopping rules, etc.? • Review of Monitoring Plan Results: Ensure that Site Monitoring results are being reviewed by investigator and events that impact subject safety or data integrity are reported per IRB requirements.

results.title: When is a DSMB needed? - One UNC Clinical Research
results.content: Home / Resources / Services / Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) / When is a DSMB needed? **A Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) is typically needed in the following situations:**. * All Phase III studies require a DSMB, except for low risk behavioral and nutritional studies. * Phase II multicenter, randomized trials require a DSMB, with the exception of low risk behavioral and nutritional studies. * Phase II trials deemed high risk require a DSMB. + As a general rule, DSMBs are necessary for clinical trials involving diseases with high mortality or morbidity, high risk interventions, and large, multicenter trials. * Single-center open-label Phase I and II clinical trials typically do not require a DSMB, as the local investigator has access to all the data. * For multicenter, high-risk Phase I clinical trials, a DSMB is generally not necessary if there are clear guidelines for stopping the trial. For example, a classic open-label dose escalation trial with objective criteria for halting dose escalation in the event of unacceptable side effects may not need a DSMB. However, if the Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (DSMP) lacks objective criteria, a DSMB may be requested. * A DSMB may not be feasible for clinical trials that are expected to enroll participants too quickly for the formation of a DSMB or for completing thorough data and safety monitoring. If you plan to use the UNC-CH DSMB to monitor a clinical trial funded by an NIH or other federal grant, please submit a copy of your grant proposal to the DSMB for review before submitting it to the funding agency. The DSMB will provide guidance on study stopping rules, appropriate study design, and the safety monitoring plan. If the DSMB agrees to oversee the trial, a letter of support outlining the DSMB’s role in monitoring the study will be provided. If you have questions about whether a DSMB is needed for your study or would like to discuss your research proposal to determine if the UNC-CH DSMB is the right resource, contact Katie Marsh. A meeting can be scheduled to review the details of your research protocol and develop a plan for monitoring study data and ensuring participant safety.
